newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bond spreads mixed on CPI selling.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bond spreads mixed on CPI selling.

text.p: Australian bond spreads finished mixed after some heavy selling on disappointment at a moderation in inflation that only matched, rather than exceeded, the market's bullish expectations.

After a strong overnight session where bonds had followed U.S. Treasuries higher and stayed there while Treasuries had eased in late New York trading, bonds continued to improve through the morning ahead of the data's release.

That strength ahead of the data saw the spread to U.S. 10-year Treasuries narrow to under 75 points, but after the inflation figures came in as expected, follow-through buying was absent and profit takers drove the spread wider, traders said.

Australia's CPI rose just 0.2 percent in the December quarter, to be 1.5 percent higher over the year. It was the lowest annual rise since the March 1994 quarter, and was slightly under median expectations.

The underlying rate, the focus of monetary policy, rose 0.4 percent to be 2.1 percent higher over the year, its lowest annual rise since the March 1995 quarter. The underlying inflation figures were spot on market expectations.

While there was disappointment on the day, the general picture of continuing low inflation meant that spreads should remain well supported, especially given the growing concerns in the U.S. market about inflation, analysts said.
"The confirmation of low inflation justifies the recent spread compression with the U.S. on the 10 year bond and justifies the RBA monetary policy action last year," Koukoulas said.
The curves continued their recent steepening trend, and the futures spread closed above 100 points for the first time in a week.
Analysts said with the short end still seeing another rate cut as likely, the bias could be for the short end to continue its outperformance, especially if U.S. sentiment remained bearish.
